desc:
The multiplicative persistence of a non-negative integer n is the number of steps needed to reach a single digit when each step replaces the number with the product of its decimal digits.

Return the multiplicative persistence of n.

n = 39   -> 39 -> 27 -> 14 -> 4, so the answer is 3
n = 7    -> already a single digit, so the answer is 0
n = 999  -> 729 -> 126 -> 12 -> 2, so the answer is 4
hints: Write a loop that replaces n with the product of its digits and counts the rounds until n has a single digit.
Extract digits with % 10 and // 10. A digit 0 makes the product 0 at once, which then ends the process.
The number of digits shrinks at each round, so the loop runs only a few times. Check for a single digit before the first round so that 0 steps is returned for small inputs.
editorial: Each round replaces the number with the product of its digits. For any number with two or more digits, that product has fewer digits than the number itself, so the value keeps shrinking and the process ends.
Inputs below 2<sup>31</sup> need only a handful of rounds, so simulating the process is the whole solution. Each round costs time proportional to the number of digits.
time: O(d) per round, a few rounds
solution:
def multiplicativePersistence(n):
    steps = 0
    while n >= 10:
        prod = 1
        m = n
        while m:
            m, d = divmod(m, 10)
            prod *= d
        n = prod
        steps += 1
    return steps
